title: Streamlined quantization profile CI + publish pipeline and automated perf-regression detection
creator: Alicia Park
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated, auditable CI pipeline that produces verified quantization profiles for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ variants, publishes signed profiles to the model catalog, and runs continuous perf + quality checks to detect regressions before and after rollout. This ticket covers the pipeline orchestration, eval harness integration, release metadata, and automated regression alerts tied into Console dashboards and rollout gating.

Why: We onboard models quickly today but lack a standardized mechanism to produce and publish per-model quant profiles with CI provenance. That causes ad-hoc manual tweaks during serving rollouts and increases risk of silent latency or quality regressions. We also need clear version-pinning semantics so customer pinning + automatic fallbacks remain predictable when we ship new profiles or runtime kernel changes.
acceptance_criteria: CI job that accepts a model artifact and emits one or more quant profiles (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ) with deterministic metadata and checksum
Automated validation runs for each profile that measure throughput, p99 latency, peak GPU memory, and a quality metric (perplexity or eval-set accuracy) against a canonical eval-set

Profiles are signed and published to the model catalog with stable identifiers and semantic profile versions (eg. qv1.2-awq), plus a manifest linking runtime compatibility (kernels/hardware) and pinning advisories
Console shows profile-level performance historicals and flags regressions when post-publish metrics exceed thresholds (configurable), with automatic rollback or canary gating hooks
Regression detector integrates with alerts (PagerDuty/Slack) and annotates the model catalog entry with the last good profile and recommended roll-forward/fallback path
Documentation and runbook for on-call and SRE describing how to interpret profile regressions and trigger manual rollbacks or hotfix profiles
tasks: Design CI workflow for quant profile generation (quant-extract + quant-validate + publish step)
Implement quant-validate harness that runs standard eval set (lm-bench-1000) and perf measurements using real runtime kernels
Add signing step and checksum metadata; extend catalog schema to accept profile artifact and compatibility labels
Bridge CI outputs to Console: profile metrics ingestion and historical charting per profile version
Implement perf-regression detector with thresholds and an enriched alert payload (include diffs and link to failing artifacts)
Create rollout gating integration: canary check that blocks model pin promotion if regression detected
Build docs: onboarding checklist, profile naming conventions, and emergency rollback playbook
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and console teams. Agreed to reuse quant-validate prototype from ENG-8302 as starting point but add deterministic eval set and perf metrics collection.
2026-02-25: Prototype CI pipeline (GitHub Actions) can produce AWQ and GPTQ profiles for Llama-2-13B. Measured baseline throughput and perplexity; initial numbers pushed to a temporary S3 bucket.

2026-03-01: Design review feedback from Claire Huang: require profile signing and manifest field 'runtime_kernel_constraints' to avoid incompatible auto-assignments. Action: add manifest schema and signing step.

2026-03-03: Implemented perf-regression detector logic in a new service 'profile-guard'. Running in staging; detects >5% throughput drop or >2% perplexity increase as regression. Initial false-positive tuning in progress.
2026-03-05: End-to-end staging run for Llama-2-70B quant variants succeeded for INT8 and AWQ; GPTQ still flaky on fp16 fallback path. Created follow-up ENG-9499 for GPTQ runtime kernel fix.
design_decisions: Prefer AWQ profiles for Llama-family models by default when quality delta < 1% and memory reduction > 20%; fallback to GPTQ only when AWQ not available or quality delta > 1%
Use semantic profile versions prefixed with 'qv' (quantization-version) and include variant tag (eg qv1.0-awq). Catalog must preserve historical profiles.
Regression thresholds: default 'throughput_drop_pct' = 5, 'ppl_increase_pct' = 2, but thresholds are configurable per-model-family in catalog metadata
Profiles must be signed by CI pipeline key to be considered 'trusted' for automatic rollout; unsigned profiles require manual approval
Profile artifacts include 'compat_kernels' list to prevent automatic assignment to unsupported runtime kernels
links: Follow-up ticket for GPTQ kernel fix: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9499-gptq-kernel-fallback-fix.json
qa_plan: Run CI pipeline against 12 diverse model artifacts (opt/llama/transformer families) in staging
Verify Console charts show per-profile throughput, p99, and quality metrics for at least 30 days of synthetic backfills
Introduce controlled regression (artificial kernel slowdown) and assert profile-guard fires alert and blocks canary promotion
Smoke test signed-profile automatic promotion and manual approval flow
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives from noisy eval sets. Mitigation: use deterministic seed, larger eval samples (lm-bench-1000), and require multiple CI runs before flagging major alerts
Risk: Catalog schema changes could break older clients. Mitigation: support backward-compatible fields and deprecation timeline + migration tool
Risk: Profile signing key compromise. Mitigation: rotate CI keys monthly and require HSM-stored signing for production 'trusted' profiles
Risk: Performance regressions during rollout. Mitigation: canary gating enforced by profile-guard and automatic fallback to last-good profile
